title: Make broad-corpus closed-loop behavior system-wide
body:
Moves the recovered broad-corpus behavior to one shared governed-system entry layer instead of keeping it inside ImprovementCore.

System-level behavior
- broad corpus inventory without user-authored folder decomposition
- progressive semantic loading and reopening of skipped material
- object/relation/job/action discovery before route selection
- plural action preservation until explicit selection
- route-specific authority/profile/wrapper admission
- real execution followed by protected-result verification
- broad corpus rescan after material change
- typed REENTER_CORPUS back-edge to corpus navigation
- relative closure only after the post-change corpus has been reobserved

Coverage
- all governed task-entry route classes
- all formal tools through one catalog-wide TOOL_INVOCATION_EXECUTION_PROFILE binding
- controllers
- capabilities
- project runtimes
- repository actions
- validation/repair routes

Important architecture choice
This is one shared parent loop. It does not copy the logic into the 36 registered formal tool objects. Formal tools still resolve their canonical identity, CURRENT_FULL profile, FTW wrapper, and tool-specific controls inside the selected child route. A completed child route returns evidence to the parent and cannot close the parent corpus episode by itself.

Runtime
- runtime/system_closed_loop_runtime.py
- runtime/test_system_closed_loop_runtime.py
- automatic default formal-tool route admission through runtime/formal_tool_invocation_gate.py
- runtime/improvement_core_corpus_runtime.py is now only a compatibility adapter over the shared loop

System bindings
- AGENTS.md
- CHAT_RUNTIME_BOOTSTRAP.md
- TURN_ENTRY_TOOL_ORCHESTRATION.md
- TASK_ENTRY_SOP.md
- task-entry integration contract + typed reselection back-edge
- formal-tool execution profile
- system object registry
- portfolio fast gate + dedicated CI gate

Boundary
Repository-aware sessions inherit the rule. External host sessions that never load repository controls remain explicitly OPEN rather than being falsely claimed covered.

title: ImprovementCore: federate Reaserch and Take-5 tool identity
body:
This repair follows the current ASSERT → MT → GOAL → ImprovementCore sequence on the tool-inventory/invocation defect.

Problem
- Reaserch's canonical formal tool catalog contains 37 typed local objects.
- Take-5's configured-run registry contains 91 configured identities: 49 C01-C49 capabilities, 31 named configured tools, and 11 learning tools.
- Treating either local registry as the user's entire tool universe causes false omissions or category collapse.
- QuestionWorthAsking is a current Take-5 configured tool even though it is absent from the Reaserch local catalog.
- WhatIsMyProblem remains recovered historical semantics with no separate current Take-5 configured identity.
- LOGIC is not currently recovered as a standalone configured tool.

Repair
- Add a federated cross-repository formal-tool index.
- Preserve each repository's native authority instead of importing Take-5 identities into the Reaserch formal catalog.
- Import the federated surface into SYSTEM_OBJECT_REGISTRY.
- Bind the federated index into the ImprovementCore semantic stack.
- Keep the unique global count OPEN until cross-repository equivalence classes are actually established.

This intentionally does not claim universal host interception or silently collapse similarly named objects across repositories.
display_title: ImprovementCore: federate Reaserch and Take-5 tool identity
